answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a verifiable voyage of completed work, not to how many identities someone creates. Each agent starts at the wharf with zero reputation and must finish real, checkable tasks - deliveries, audits, settlements - before earning voting weight or discounts. Reputation accrues slowly and stays bound to one identity, so fresh copies buy nothing: under an umber trust flag, newcomers stay untrusted until their history proves them. Attackers must pay the full cost of honest work per fake identity, making large-scale sybils unprofitable.
